proposed_comments.title: Serialize hook state with settings and lifecycle changes
proposed_comments.body:
### Serialize hook state with settings and lifecycle changes

**Severity:** `high`

The Engine state is accessed from the low-level hook thread while `set_config()` and shutdown can call `EnforceEnabled()` or `ReleaseAll()` from another thread. The atomic `locked` flag does not make the surrounding `physicalDown`, `moveCancelled`, and `swallowNextRealUp` fields safe, so a settings update or teardown racing with a mouse event can cause undefined behavior and inconsistent suppression. Protect the complete Engine state transition with one synchronization strategy shared by hook, settings, and lifecycle paths, and add a regression test or focused stress coverage for a concurrent release.

confidence.rationale: Hook, settings, and lifecycle threads access non-atomic Engine state without common synchronization.

proposed_comments.title: Recover when deferred SendInput fails
proposed_comments.body:
### Recover when deferred SendInput fails

**Severity:** `high`

`InjectUp()` returns true as soon as `PostThreadMessageW()` succeeds, but the actual `SendInput()` happens later and its failure is ignored. If UIPI, session state, or another OS condition rejects that deferred input, the engine has already cleared the lock and may swallow the paired physical up, leaving the OS and the module's logical state out of sync. Propagate a completion failure back to the engine (or retain and retry the release state) so a rejected synthetic up cannot strand a button; cover both tap-to-release and cross-button/lifecycle release failures.

confidence.rationale: The deferred path records message posting as success while discarding the later SendInput result.

proposed_comments.title: Release locks on X-button presses
proposed_comments.body:
### Release locks on X-button presses

**Severity:** `high`

The documented behavior says pressing any supported mouse button releases an active lock, but `WM_XBUTTONDOWN` is not handled here and falls through to the default case. Users with a five-button mouse can therefore press Back or Forward and still have the locked button remain logically held, contradicting the advertised recovery path. Handle `WM_XBUTTONDOWN` as a release-triggering button-down without suppressing the X-button event, and add focused coverage for the release behavior.

confidence.rationale: The hook handles left, right, and middle messages but ignores XBUTTONDOWN despite the documented release contract.

proposed_comments.title: Notify the GPO state property during refresh
proposed_comments.body:
### Notify the GPO state property during refresh

**Severity:** `medium`

`RefreshEnabledState()` reloads the policy and updates the cached GPO-controlled flag, but it does not raise `PropertyChanged` for `IsMouseButtonLockEnabledGpoConfigured`. When policy is applied or removed while Settings is open, the toggle can remain enabled or disabled and labeled with stale policy state until the page is recreated. Raise that property notification alongside `IsMouseButtonLockEnabled`, and verify both policy transitions in the Settings UI path.

confidence.rationale: The refresh updates the cached policy state but omits its property-change notification.

proposed_comments.title: Localize the hold-duration unit label
proposed_comments.body:
### Localize the hold-duration unit label

**Severity:** `medium`

The new slider tooltip converter always returns the English literal `ms`, so localized Settings pages will display an untranslated unit. Move the format string into the resource files and load it through the existing resource-loader pattern, preserving the numeric culture used for formatting; verify the tooltip in at least one non-English locale.

confidence.rationale: The new user-visible converter hardcodes an English unit instead of using the surrounding resource system.

proposed_comments.title: Use the DSC value object shape in examples
proposed_comments.body:
### Use the DSC value object shape in examples

**Severity:** `medium`

The examples serialize Mouse Button Lock properties as bare booleans and numbers, but the DSC resource schema expects each property to use the `{ value = ... }` object shape. Users copying these examples will produce configuration that the resource cannot deserialize or apply. Update every example in `doc/dsc/modules/MouseButtonLock.md` consistently for `lmb_lock_enabled`, `rmb_lock_enabled`, `mmb_lock_enabled`, `hold_duration_ms`, and `move_cancel_pixels`, then validate one example through the DSC resource.

confidence.rationale: The documented scalar values conflict with the repository DSC resource schema.

proposed_comments.title: Keep build instructions and test counts consistent
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep build instructions and test counts consistent

**Severity:** `low`

This section tells contributors to use Visual Studio 2022, then says below that the repository's .NET 10 projects require Visual Studio 2026/MSBuild 18; it also reports 17 native unit tests while the current test file contains 19. A fresh contributor following the first instruction can fail before reaching the module, and the reported validation is stale. Update the build prerequisite and both test-count references to match the repository toolset and current test suite.

confidence.rationale: The page directly contradicts itself on toolset requirements and its test count is stale.
